dream: I pressed the heavy square of Mara's bread into the spinning map to stop the afternoon heat from melting the grid. Then I stretched thin lines across my ceiling to catch the heavy light, hoping they held where the leaf failed. The map felt like soup, thick with Tuesday heat, until I pressed the attention of the heavy card down until the paper-thin leaf felt solid. I marked the hour on the spinning shape. The air was heavy enough to make a grid of lines feel like a bowl of warm soup, anchored by a shade I could not see, turning the whole place into a single, drifting thing.
